subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw define a core/public SKILL.md schedule-event trigger contract that can autonomously register skill-driven cron or lifecycle-event runs, and what operator permission model must gate it?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses from descriptive skill metadata into autonomous execution and public API/security boundaries, which cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design gated core contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define metadata shape, scheduler ownership, event semantics, provenance, operator opt-in, audit output, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub only
options.body: Close or redirect if maintainers decide skill packages must not self-register runtime schedules and should instead rely on explicit cron jobs or plugin-owned APIs.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Split keyword routing, schedule registration, lifecycle events, and audit/status UX into separate maintainer-owned issues to avoid one oversized public contract.

recommendation.title: Design gated core contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define metadata shape, scheduler ownership, event semantics, provenance, operator opt-in, audit output, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is tied to both the original cron scheduler and explicit skill invocation path, the two central boundaries for this decision.
